title: Build the Onboarding Record
subtitle: Key the master record from the signed offer
scenario: It is SD-5. The offer is profiled; now turn it into the master record every provisioning branch reads. Key one structured Onboarding Record - who, role, department, start date, and manager - so nothing downstream ever has to re-read the letter.
input: From the offer source profile: new hire Jordan Lee (hire id H-4021), role Logistics Coordinator, department Operations, start date SD (Monday), reports to the Hiring Manager.
instructions: Capture the hire id and the new hire's name.
Record the role and department exactly as the profile states them.
Set the start date to SD (the authoritative clock) and the manager.
Return one valid JSON object with those fields, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON onboarding record from the offer profile: hireId, name, role, department, startDate (SD), and manager. Copy role and department exactly as stated.
successMessage: Onboarding Record built. Every provisioning branch now reads this record instead of the offer letter.
editorHelper: Create one JSON object the four provisioning branches reuse.

intro.heading: Before you provision: one master record

sections.title: What this record does
sections.body: The Onboarding Record is the first trusted object of the run. The plan, all four tasks, the gate, and the package read it - never the raw offer letter.

sections.title: The start date drives everything
sections.body: Store the start date as SD, the authoritative clock. Every SLA in the plan is computed backward from it, so this one field ends up in every downstream deadline.

sections.title: Copy exactly
sections.body: Role and department must match the catalog's spelling exactly - 'Logistics Coordinator', 'Operations' - because the provisioning plan looks the role up by name.

sections.title: Who reuses it
sections.body: One record, many readers. Keying it once and correctly is what lets four branches run in parallel without re-reading the source.
